changes: Vijñāneśvara: role reduced to 'commentator' (he wrote the Ṛjumitākṣarā, a commentary on the Yājñavalkyasmṛti, not the root text); evidence trimmed
Date: tithi normalised to ṣaṣṭhī; note added that Phālguna of VS 1825 falls in Feb/Mar 1769 CE
Notes expanded with other possible ways to read the garbled scribal phrase

notes: The colophon reads 'saṃvat 2825', which is clearly a slip for VS 1825. The catalogue field says SAM 1825, which agrees. VS 1825 − 57 = 1768 CE, but Phālguna of that year would fall in Feb/Mar 1769 CE. The scribal phrase 'brāhmaṇabālūprakaraṇājñātībhūṇakṛṣṇalalāṭamadhye' is badly garbled. The best guess is a brahmin named Bālū as scribe. Other readings are possible: 'Bālū' might be part of a longer name (e.g. Bālūpra-…), 'jñātī' may mean caste/kin group, and '…kṛṣṇalalāṭamadhye' may name a place of copying, but none of this can be identified with confidence. Vijñāneśvara's father, Padmanābha (Bhāradvāja gotra), is named only in the author's colophon and has nothing to do with this copy.
